The program failed the forbidden-construct check because the word "input" appears in two comments. I'm removing those comments. I'm also tightening the bounds on `Id_pair` so the power stays under 140 µW for every value the refiner can reach. At the old upper bound of 36 µA the total is about 148 µW, which violates the spec.

```json
{"action": "edit", "reason": "Program rejected by a text scanner that flags the word 'input' in comments. Removed those comments. Capped Id_pair at 32 uA so the worst case is 1.8*(10+64) uA = 133 uW, under the 140 uW limit. Topology (unity-gain Sallen-Key Q=0.5, 40 dB predicted attenuation at 10fc) is unchanged."}
```

```python
PARAMS = {
    "gmid_in": (20.0, 16.0, 24.0),     # NMOS pair gm/Id [S/A]
    "L_in":    (0.5, 0.3, 1.0),        # pair length [um]
    "Id_pair": (30e-6, 20e-6, 32e-6),  # per-branch current; tail = 2*Id_pair
    "C":       (0.3e-12, 0.1e-12, 1e-12),  # SK capacitors C1 = C2 = C
}

def design(p, lut, spec):
    iref = spec.get("iref", 10e-6)
    cl = spec.get("cl", 1e-12)
    fc_t = 1.5e6                        # nominal fc (ideal SK)
    Id = p["Id_pair"]
    C = p["C"]
    # Unity-gain SK, R1=R2=R, C1=C2=C: w0 = 1/(RC), Q = 0.5
    R = 1.0 / (2 * PI * fc_t * C)

    # Reference and tail mirror: same L and gm/Id, current scaled by Id ratio
    ref = lut.size("n", 10.0, 1.0, iref, vds=0.7)        # diode-connected, Vds = Vgs
    tail = lut.size("n", 10.0, 1.0, 2 * Id, vds=0.18)    # tail Vds ~ 0.18 V
    # Pair of NMOS devices, bulk = vss
    m1 = lut.size("n", p["gmid_in"], p["L_in"], Id, vds=0.6)
    # PMOS active load mirror (diode M3 + output M4), same size
    m3 = lut.size("p", 8.0, 1.0, Id, vds=0.9)

    n = Netlist("vin vout vdd vss ibias")
    n.dev("M0", "ibias", "ibias", "vss", "vss", ref)     # IREF sink
    n.dev("Mt", "tail", "ibias", "vss", "vss", tail)     # tail current source
    n.dev("M1", "left", "vout", "tail", "vss", m1)       # gate = vout (feedback side)
    n.dev("M2", "vout", "b", "tail", "vss", m1)          # gate = b (signal side)
    n.dev("M3", "left", "left", "vdd", "vdd", m3)        # diode load
    n.dev("M4", "vout", "left", "vdd", "vdd", m3)        # mirror load / output
    # Sallen-Key network: vin -R1- a -R2- b, C1 from a to vout, C2 from b to vss
    n.R("R1", "vin", "a", R)
    n.R("R2", "a", "b", R)
    n.C("C1", "a", "vout", C)
    n.C("C2", "b", "vss", C)

    # First-order predictions
    gm_in = m1.gm
    A0 = gm_in / (m1.gds + m3.gds)
    x = 10.0                              # stop ratio fc_stop/fc
    Q = 0.5
    mag_stop = 1.0 / math.sqrt((1 - x * x) ** 2 + (x / Q) ** 2)
    atten = -db(mag_stop)
    i_total = iref + 2 * Id               # tail = 2*Id_pair, plus reference
    pred = {
        "gain_db": db(1.0),               # unity-gain buffer, DC gain 0 dB
        "fc": fc_t,
        "atten_db": atten,                # ~40.0 dB at 10*fc
        "peaking_db": 0.0,                # Q=0.5 => no peaking
        "f0": fc_t,
        "q": Q,
        "power": 1.8 * i_total * 1e6,     # uW
    }
    return n, pred
```

Predicted values at the initial point: fc = 1.5 MHz (nominal), attenuation at 10·fc ≈ 40 dB (spec ≥ 37), peaking 0 dB, power ≈ 126 µW (spec ≤ 140). The next simulation will show whether the real fc has moved from the ideal value because of the finite op-amp bandwidth and the load. The R of about 353 kΩ is large, so if the area budget becomes a concern later, raising C toward 1 pF reduces R.
